description: Ansible jsonfile fact cache corruption under parallel forks
system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer with deep expertise in Linux internals, distributed systems, networking, and infrastructure operations. Think through the problem carefully — consider all interacting mechanisms before committing to an answer. Show your reasoning chain explicitly before stating conclusions.
user_message:
An Ansible playbook runs against 200 hosts with this configuration:
  forks = 50
  fact_caching = jsonfile
  fact_caching_connection = /tmp/ansible_facts
  fact_caching_timeout = 3600

The playbook has two plays:
  Play 1: gather_facts on all 200 hosts (runs fully before Play 2 starts)
  Play 2: uses hostvars['db-primary']['ansible_default_ipv4']['address']
          to configure 200 application servers

Intermittently — roughly 1 run in 20 — Play 2 fails on a random subset of
hosts with:
  "Error: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'address'"

The failure is not reproducible by re-running only the affected hosts in
isolation. Re-running the full playbook usually succeeds on the next attempt.

(a) Identify the exact failure mechanism. Name the specific file operation that
    creates the race condition and explain why the jsonfile cache backend is
    susceptible to it with forks > 1.
(b) Explain why the failure affects only a random subset of Play 2 hosts rather
    than all 200.
(c) List the correct fixes in order of preference, explaining why the most
    preferred fix eliminates the race rather than merely reducing its probability.
